newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar trading slows by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar trading slows by close.

text.p: Trading in LIFFE white sugar futures had slowed by the close from the busier levels seen earlier in the day.
Prices had rallied from the day's lows but were still $1.90 to $0.70 a tonne down in the more active nearer positions. Turnover totalled 4,811 lots.
Traders said the fall in white sugar futures during most of Wednesday was halted in the late afternoon by a rally in New York raws futures.

In the morning a bout of hedge selling ahead of the weekly EU tender, where subsidies for a sizeable tonnage were expected, had narrowed the December/March spread to $0.50 a tonne before renewed support developed and it ended the day at around $1.
When news of the EU's 104,350 tonnes release circulated it had been discounted and traders were watching New York.

In physicals Tunisia bought one cargo of whites at a scheduled tender but there was no news from Syria where authorities were due to be replying to offers of one cargo of raws and one whites for late Nov/late Dec arrival.
Paris white sugar ended with December at $304.50 a tonne, down $1.10 from Tuesday.
